evidence.quote: Redwood Peak Construction Co.
evidence.rationale: Preamble identifies Redwood Peak Construction Co. as "Contractor".

evidence.quote: Precision Roofing & Sheet Metal
evidence.rationale: Preamble identifies Precision Roofing & Sheet Metal as "Subcontractor".

evidence.quote: City of Santa Rosa
evidence.rationale: Recitals identify the City of Santa Rosa as "Owner".

evidence.quote: Fire Station 5 Replacement
evidence.rationale: Recitals name the project as Fire Station 5 Replacement.

evidence.quote: This Subcontract is governed by the laws of the State of California.
evidence.rationale: Section 16.1 selects California law.

evidence.quote: This is a pay-when-paid provision governing when payment is due.
evidence.rationale: Section 6.3 makes Owner payment a timing condition only and says payment becomes due within a reasonable time if Owner fails to pay for reasons not attributable to Subcontractor.

evidence.quote: within seven (7) days after Contractor's receipt of the corresponding progress payment
evidence.rationale: Section 6.3 states seven days after Contractor's receipt of the Owner's payment.

evidence.quote: Contractor and Subcontractor expressly agree in writing that Owner's payment to Contractor is a condition of the timing of Contractor's payment to Subcontractor.
evidence.rationale: A specific seven-day period is written in Section 6.3, and the parties expressly agree to it in writing.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall retain five percent (5%) of the amount due on each progress payment to Subcontractor as retention.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.1 sets retention at 5%, which is 500 bps.

release_condition.value: upon both (a) Final Completion of the Subcontract Work and (b) Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner

evidence.quote: Retention becomes payable to Subcontractor upon both (a) Final Completion of the Subcontract Work and (b) Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.2 states both release conditions.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall pay the retention to Subcontractor within ten (10) days after the later of those two events.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.2 sets ten days after the later of the two events.

evidence.quote: Before Contractor makes each progress payment, Subcontractor shall deliver to Contractor Subcontractor's own conditional waiver and release on progress payment
evidence.rationale: Section 8.1 requires a conditional progress waiver before each progress payment.

evidence.quote: After Subcontractor receives each progress payment, Subcontractor shall deliver to Contractor Subcontractor's own unconditional waiver and release on progress payment
evidence.rationale: Section 8.2 requires an unconditional progress waiver after each payment is received.

evidence.quote: All waivers and releases delivered under this Article must be on the exact statutory forms prescribed by the California Civil Code, without modification
evidence.rationale: Section 8.4 requires the exact statutory forms; Sections 8.1-8.3 cite Civil Code 8132, 8134, 8136 and 8138.

evidence.quote: Contractor may set off and deduct Backcharges from any amount otherwise due to Subcontractor under this Subcontract.
evidence.rationale: Section 9.1 permits Backcharge setoff, with written notice.

evidence.quote: Contractor may withhold from any payment an amount sufficient to cover the cost of correcting defective or nonconforming Subcontract Work that Subcontractor has not corrected.
evidence.rationale: Section 9.2 permits withholding for uncorrected defective work.

evidence.quote: Contractor will pay only for materials incorporated into the Work, and will not pay for materials stored on or off the Project site that have not yet been installed.
evidence.rationale: Section 6.4 expressly excludes payment for stored materials on or off site.

anomalies.description: The waiver article requires only Subcontractor's own waivers. There is no requirement for conditional or unconditional releases from sub-subcontractors or suppliers, which leaves lower-tier lien and stop payment notice exposure unaddressed.
The fallback when Owner does not pay is an undefined 'reasonable time' rather than a fixed number of days, so the payment due date becomes uncertain.

evidence.quote: If Owner fails to pay Contractor for reasons not attributable to Subcontractor, Contractor's obligation to pay Subcontractor for approved work becomes due within a reasonable time.
evidence.rationale: The fallback when Owner does not pay is an undefined 'reasonable time' rather than a fixed number of days, so the payment due date becomes uncertain.

anomalies.description: Retention release depends on Final Completion, which requires acceptance by both Contractor and Owner, and on Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner. Release timing therefore depends on Owner action.

evidence.quote: has been completed and accepted by Contractor and Owner
evidence.rationale: Retention release depends on Final Completion, which requires acceptance by both Contractor and Owner, and on Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner. Release timing therefore depends on Owner action.

anomalies.description: Contractor may deduct Article 9 withholdings directly from retention when it becomes payable.

evidence.quote: Contractor may deduct from retention any amounts it is entitled to withhold under Article 9 at the time the retention becomes payable.
evidence.rationale: Contractor may deduct Article 9 withholdings directly from retention when it becomes payable.

anomalies.description: Withholding rights extend beyond defective work to missing documents, Owner liquidated damages and any material breach.

evidence.quote: Contractor may also withhold payment for: (a) Subcontractor's failure to submit certified payroll records or other documents required by the Subcontract Documents; (b) liquidated damages assessed by Owner to the extent caused by Subcontractor; and (c) Subcontractor's material breach of this Subcontract.
evidence.rationale: Withholding rights extend beyond defective work to missing documents, Owner liquidated damages and any material breach.

anomalies.description: Contractor may decline to process payment until a properly completed waiver is received, so waiver defects can delay payment.

evidence.quote: Contractor may decline to process a payment until a properly completed waiver is received.
evidence.rationale: Contractor may decline to process payment until a properly completed waiver is received, so waiver defects can delay payment.

anomalies.description: Payment on termination for convenience is limited to amounts Contractor recovers from Owner, which shifts Owner non-payment risk to Subcontractor for that scenario.

evidence.quote: plus reasonable demobilization costs, to the extent Contractor recovers those amounts from Owner.
evidence.rationale: Payment on termination for convenience is limited to amounts Contractor recovers from Owner, which shifts Owner non-payment risk to Subcontractor for that scenario.

anomalies.description: Monetary recovery for delay is limited to amounts Contractor actually recovers from Owner.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor's monetary recovery for delay is limited to the amount, if any, that Contractor actually recovers from Owner on Subcontractor's behalf.
evidence.rationale: Monetary recovery for delay is limited to amounts Contractor actually recovers from Owner.

anomalies.description: On termination for default, all further payment is suspended until the Subcontract Work is complete.

evidence.quote: On termination for default, Subcontractor is not entitled to further payment until the Subcontract Work is complete.
evidence.rationale: On termination for default, all further payment is suspended until the Subcontract Work is complete.
